description: Host-side thermal and power for the DGX trays, from node-exporter hwmon. GPU core/HBM temperature, GPU power and the DCGM throttle/violation counters are owned by the GPU Health board and are deliberately not duplicated here.

options.content:
Host-side thermal & power. Everything on this board comes from node-exporter hwmon on the 1,898 DGX trays: chassis temperature sensors (NIC ASIC, NVMe, ACPI zone), each sensor's own vendor critical limit, and the six ACPI module power meters per tray.
Every tile has the table underneath it built from the identical query, so a headline number and its worklist can never disagree.
GPU core / HBM temperature, GPU power draw, clock throttling and the DCGM violation counters are not repeated here — the GPU Health board is their single source of truth.

panels.title: Tray temperature sensors — hwmon, each reading referenced to its own vendor critical limit

panels.description:
max(node_hwmon_temp_celsius) over the selected SUs and racks.

L2: the table 'Hottest tray sensors — top 50' directly below uses the same selector and the same $su/$rack filter; its first row IS this number.
panels.title: Hottest tray sensor

panels.description:
count of hwmon sensors whose (critical − current) headroom is under 15 °C.

L2: 'Sensors within 15 °C of vendor critical — the exact sensors' below is the same expression rendered as a table; its row count IS this number.
panels.title: Sensors within 15 °C of vendor critical

panels.description:
count of distinct racks with at least one hwmon temperature sensor reporting.

L2: 'Tray-sensor coverage by rack' below lists exactly these racks; its row count IS this number.
panels.title: Racks reporting tray sensors

panels.description:
count of distinct hwmon chip classes (mlx5 NIC ASIC, nvme, acpitz) currently publishing a temperature.

L2: 'Sensor classes' below lists exactly these classes; its row count IS this number.
panels.title: Sensor classes reporting

panels.description: topk(50, node_hwmon_temp_celsius) with the hwmon chip class joined in. Same selector and same $su/$rack filter as the tile above, so the top row equals it exactly.
panels.title: Hottest tray sensors — top 50 · row 1 is the “Hottest tray sensor” tile

panels.description: The identical expression behind the 'Sensors within 15 °C of vendor critical' tile, rendered as a table. The value column is the remaining headroom in °C, lowest first.
panels.title: Sensors within 15 °C of vendor critical — the exact sensors (rows = the tile above)

panels.description: Same selector as the 'Racks reporting tray sensors' tile, grouped to one row per rack. 'Trays reporting' reads 18 on a full GB300 rack — anything lower is a tray whose node-exporter is not publishing hwmon.

targets.expr: count by (rack, su) (count by (rack, su, node) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{su=~"$su",rack=~"$rack"}))

panels.title: Tray-sensor coverage by rack — one row per rack (rows = “Racks reporting tray sensors”)

panels.description: Same selector as the 'Sensor classes reporting' tile, grouped by hwmon chip class. acpitz publishes no vendor critical, so its headroom cell is empty by design.

targets.expr: min by (chip_name) ((((node_hwmon_temp_crit_celsius{su=~"$su",rack=~"$rack"} > 0) - ignoring(__name__) node_hwmon_temp_celsius{su=~"$su",rack=~"$rack"})) * on(instance,chip) group_left(chip_name) node_hwmon_chip_names)

panels.title: Sensor classes — one row per class (rows = “Sensor classes reporting”)

panels.description: max(node_hwmon_temp_celsius) per hwmon chip class, one line each. The chip selectors below reproduce the classes in the 'Sensor classes' table exactly (mlx5 22,444 · nvme 17,082 · acpitz 51,246 sensors) and are used in place of the chip_name join, which costs ~4 s on a 6 h range and got the panel cancelled on scroll.
panels.title: Hottest tray sensor by class

panels.description: L2 for the trend above. topk(20, max_over_time(node_hwmon_temp_celsius[$__range])) by (chip_name), same $su/$rack filter, raw samples. Filter the Class column and the top row equals that line’s legend Max exactly — verified mlx5 104.0, nvme 79.9, acpitz 93.7 °C. Per-class topk is used so every line is backed: a plain top-50 was entirely WH1H6 and contained no nvme row at all.
panels.title: Peak sensor temperature over the selected window — top 20 per class · each class’s top row is that line’s “Max” in the legend above
Tray module power — hwmon ACPI power meters (six meters per tray)

panels.description:
sum of every hwmon ACPI power meter in scope.

L2: 'Module power by tray' below is the same selector grouped per tray — the table's column total, shown in its footer, IS this number.
panels.title: Tray module-meter power

panels.description:
count of trays publishing at least one hwmon ACPI power meter.

L2: 'Module power by tray' below — its row count IS this number.
panels.title: Trays reporting module meters

panels.description:
max over trays of the summed module meters.

L2: 'Module power by tray' below — its first row IS this number.
panels.title: Highest tray module power

panels.description:
max of (module average watts ÷ that same module's hwmon power cap).

L2: 'Modules closest to their hwmon cap' below — its first row IS this number.
panels.title: Highest module load vs its hwmon cap

panels.description: sum by (node, rack, su) of node_hwmon_power_average_watt — the exact expression the three power tiles above reduce. The footer shows the column total so it can be read against the kW tile without leaving the page.
panels.title: Module power by tray — rows = “Trays reporting”, footer total = the kW tile, row 1 = the W tile

panels.description: topk(50) of (module average watts ÷ that module's hwmon power cap). Only meters that publish a cap can appear; the remaining meters have no cap to be compared against.
panels.title: Modules closest to their hwmon cap — top 50 · row 1 is the “Highest module load” tile

panels.description: sum by (su) of node_hwmon_power_average_watt — one line per SU, so every contributor to the fleet total is named in the legend.
panels.title: Tray module power by SU

title: Thermal & Power — Tray Sensors & Module Meters
